title: Cherokee forced removal
why_famous: The U.S. government forced Cherokee communities from their homelands, causing widespread death and dispossession.
route_summary: Representative Cherokee northern forced-removal corridor from the Fort Cass-area camps in Tennessee through Kentucky, Illinois, Missouri, and Arkansas to Indian Territory.
source_title: National Park Service: Trail of Tears route map

additional_sources.title: NPS National Register documentation — Cherokee northern removal route
additional_sources.note: Records eleven northern-route detachments, nine departing camps near Fort Cass/Camp Ross, and the separate Taylor variation.

geometry_note: Represents the northern overland removal corridor, not one person's track or every detachment. NPS records nine of eleven northern-route detachments leaving from camps near Fort Cass and Camp Ross; two used the Taylor variation near Chattanooga. Red Clay is a Cherokee homeland council site, not a documented origin for this corridor, so it is not plotted as its first route anchor. Place-to-place connectors are schematic, pending careful tracing of the NPS route GIS; the NPS maps multiple other land and water routes.

title: Oregon Trail migrations
why_famous: A major settler wagon corridor to the Pacific Northwest with profound effects on Native nations.
route_summary: Representative main corridor from Independence to The Dalles; before 1846 emigrants had to descend the Columbia by water toward Fort Vancouver, and afterward river travel remained an alternative to the Barlow wagon road to Oregon City.
source_title: National Park Service: historic trail GIS
geometry_note: The Independence–The Dalles wagon corridor now follows 218 sampled vertices of the NPS approximate designated Oregon National Historic Trail GIS alignment. Nine named controls were matched to nearby mapped vertices (maximum offset 3.2 km); two multipart joins under 55 m were inferred. The 1:100,000-scale designation is not a verified individual emigrant trace. Columbia water travel and the post-1846 Barlow Road remain schematic alternatives, not a single journey.

additional_sources.title: Data.gov — Oregon National Historic Trail feature service metadata
additional_sources.note: Describes the NPS dataset as an approximate designated route rather than a measured emigrant track.
